# Tests of the packages that .github/workflows/go-macos.yml gates that cannot
# pass on its macOS runner for host reasons, not code reasons, and tests that
# skip themselves on it.
#
# The format and the rules are those of environment-only-tests.txt beside
# this file, which .github/ci/go_test_gate.py reads and documents. The
# workflow passes the gate the package pattern in TESTED_PACKAGES, and every
# line here must name a package that the pattern names. The step "Test" of
# that workflow skips the entries and runs everything else in those
# packages. The step "Listed tests still fail" fails the run when an entry
# passes, skips itself or does not run on that runner, so a change that
# makes a listed test pass on macOS has to delete its line in the same
# change.
#
# The entries come first in this file, and the lines for tests that skip
# themselves after them, under their own heading.
#
# The way to shorten this list is to port a test so that it passes on a
# macOS runner without weakening it.

# Remote Alpha operator-host tests in the scripts package.

# The test process must run as the account named "ds", and the runner has no
# such account. The first two tests are listed whole for the reason that
# environment-only-tests.txt gives for them: the TLS status bootstrap refuses
# a caller that is not "ds" at its first identity check, so a subtest that
# expects a refusal passes without reaching the check it is named for.
execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaESServiceTLSStatusFailureWitnessBootstrapOwnedTerminal
execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaESServiceTLSStatusRootLoadedStageCustody
execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaESServiceTLSStatusStageFIFOSubstitution
execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaOperatorRecoverySessionESTLSStatusStageFIFORefusal
execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaP0tGrammarDiagnosticBootstrapLifecycleComposition
execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaP0tGrammarDiagnosticPriorReaderCloseSuppression
execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaP0tGrammarDiagnosticV2VersionedBootstrap

# On macOS, /var and /tmp are symbolic links to /private/var and
# /private/tmp. The box helpers that these tests run check every folder on
# the way to an output or backup folder and refuse a symbolic link there.
# The helpers run only on the box, where /var and /tmp are folders. The first
# four tests use a default folder under /var/tmp. The last two expect a
# refusal that names /var/tmp or /var/log, and get the refusal for the link
# /var first; the other subtests of the second one pass.
execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaESBinaryDeploymentCheckOnlyIsDefaultAndNonMutating
execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaESConfigTLSPrepRecordsDSSecurityWarningsWithoutFailing
execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaESConfigTLSPrepRejectsPreexistingBroadPrepAccount
execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaVaultServiceUserMigrationApplyRequiresReadyPreflight
execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaOutputDirRefusesASharedStickyFolderAsTheArtifactFolder
execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaVaultServiceUserMigrationPlanRefusesPathsOutsideVault/log_file_in_a_shared_system_directory

# The output folder check opens each folder with O_PATH, which needs no read
# permission on it. macOS has no O_PATH, so the check falls back to O_RDONLY
# and cannot open a folder that it may not read, which these tests expect it
# to check. The second test runs the check inside the summary-path prepare
# command of scripts/remote_alpha_operator.sh, a box command, through a fake
# ssh on the host.
execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaOutputDirChecksFoldersItCannotRead
execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaOperatorPrepareSummaryPathHandsOverAnUnreadableFolder

# These tests run the summary-path prepare command of
# scripts/remote_alpha_operator.sh through a fake ssh on the host, with a
# summary folder that the helper user cannot write. The command hands that
# folder over with 'chmod 0750 -- "${summary_dir}"' at
# scripts/remote_alpha_operator.sh:997, which is the chmod of GNU coreutils.
# The chmod of macOS takes its first operand as the mode and every later one
# as a file, "--" included, so the command stops with
# summary_parent_chmod_failed. The command runs only on the box.
execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaOperatorRecoverySessionVaultWorkloadAuthBootstrapPrepareSummaryPathUsesBoundedRemoteCommand
execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaOperatorRecoverySessionVaultWorkloadAuthBootstrapPrepareRunsBeforeHelperExecution

# The box helper that these tests run, require_vault_owned_raft_dir in
# scripts/remote_alpha_reset_disposable_vault.sh:410, reads the owner of the
# raft directory with "sudo stat -c '%U'", which is the stat of GNU
# coreutils. The stat of macOS has no -c. The helper runs only on the box.
# The tests themselves read the owner with the stat of the host. The other
# subtests of the second test pass.
execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaResetDisposableVaultNeverFollowsALinkAboveTheRaftDirectory
execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaResetDisposableVaultRefusesUnsafeRaftStates/raft_directory_of_the_Vault_account

# The test builds esconfigcheck for the host and reads its build information
# with go_build_info of the ES upgrade helper, which reads the 64-bit
# little-endian ELF files of the box and refuses anything else. On macOS the
# build is a Mach-O file.
execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaUpgradeESReadsGoBuildInfoLikeGoVersion

# The ES upgrade issues Nomad's TLS material with nomad_tls_issue of
# scripts/70_linux_setup.sh and then checks it with nomad_tls_material_ok,
# the setup's own check. Both use GNU coreutils: the issuer moves each file
# into place with "mv -T", which the mv of macOS does not have ("mv: illegal
# option -- T"), so every apply that issues material stops with
# "nomad_tls_issue failed" and rolls back; and the check reads the server
# key's mode with "stat -c '%a'", which the stat of macOS does not have, so
# it fails for any material, and check calls a host with Nomad's TLS
# directory "present, but its material fails". The setup script and the
# upgrade run only on the Linux box. The tests below each reach the issuer
# or the check with material it should accept. The first is listed whole:
# its subtest "the TLS key is readable by others" expects the check to
# refuse, so on macOS it passes without reaching the key-mode check it is
# named for, as stat -c fails first. go.yml runs all of them.
execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaUpgradeESCheckRefusesWhatItWasNotWrittenFor
execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaUpgradeESApply
execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaUpgradeESApplyRollsBackOnFailure
execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaUpgradeESApplyRollsBackWhenInterrupted
execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaUpgradeESRollbackFailuresAreReported
execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaUpgradeESApplySurvivesALostSession


# Tests that skip themselves on the runner.
#
# The rules of environment-only-tests.txt for these lines hold here: the
# tests that skip themselves on the runner must be exactly the tests named
# below, and a line has to go when its test no longer skips itself there.
# The step "Listed tests pass as root" of go.yml reads only
# environment-only-tests.txt, and this workflow has no such step, so this
# workflow does not run the lines below as root. Those of them that
# environment-only-tests.txt also names run as root on Linux in go.yml.
# Each group says what its tests need that the runner does not have.

# Interfaces of the Linux kernel that macOS does not have. The TLS status
# collector and its stage run only on the box. The first five tests need PID
# namespaces (os.unshare, os.setns and os.CLONE_NEWPID), the next four read
# /proc, the next five need os.waitid, which the Python of macOS does not
# offer, and the two firewall subtests read /proc/net/tcp.
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaESServiceTLSStatusChildNamespaceRealCollectorDeath
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaESServiceTLSStatusChildNamespaceRealDeafAnchor
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaESServiceTLSStatusChildNamespaceRealDescendants
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaESServiceTLSStatusChildNamespaceRealKernel
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaESServiceTLSStatusChildNamespaceRealSiblings
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaESServiceTLSStatusChildNamespaceAnchorProcess
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaESServiceTLSStatusProcessIdentityLiveProcesses
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaESServiceTLSStatusProcessIdentityThreadExecStaysPresent
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaESServiceTLSStatusUnrelatedProcessNameDoesNotHoldCleanup
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaOperatorHealthcheckTLSStatusNoninteractiveDescendantRealCollectorDeath
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaOperatorHealthcheckTLSStatusNoninteractiveDescendantRealCrowd
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaOperatorHealthcheckTLSStatusNoninteractiveDescendantRealKernel
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaOperatorHealthcheckTLSStatusNoninteractiveDescendantRealProbeRefusesAChild
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaOperatorHealthcheckTLSStatusNoninteractiveDescendantRealProcessLimit
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaHostFirewallHostVaultSource/ipv4
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaHostFirewallHostVaultSource/ipv6

# The host firewall's real-kernel and real-sshd tests, for the reason that
# environment-only-tests.txt gives: the first three build network namespaces
# and load nftables, the fourth runs sshd -t, and all four need root. The
# runner runs the tests without root.
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaHostFirewallRealKernelApplyConfirmRollback
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaHostFirewallRealKernelBridgeIsolation
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaHostFirewallRealKernelTraffic
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaHostFirewallSSHDDropInWithRealSSHD

# Tests against a real SPIRE and a real Vault. go.yml installs the pinned
# Linux releases on its runner; this workflow does not, and the SPIRE
# release is a Linux build.
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaSPIREAgentPinAgainstRealSPIRE
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaSPIREAgentRecoverAgainstRealSPIRE
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaVaultWorkloadAuthBootstrapSignalsWithRealVault
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaVaultWorkloadAuthBootstrapUnsealKeyWithRealVault

# The ES upgrade against a real Nomad, which the test starts on the box's own
# nomad.hcl. That config's client settings are Linux's, so the test skips
# itself on any other system before it looks for the nomad binary and
# passwordless sudo. The upgrade runs only on the box. go.yml runs the test.
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestRemoteAlphaUpgradeESMovesARealNomadToHTTPS

# The signing key rotation makes its keys with the box's /usr/bin/openssl,
# which is OpenSSL. The /usr/bin/openssl of macOS is LibreSSL, whose genpkey
# has no Ed25519, so the test that runs the rotation with the machine's own
# /usr/bin/openssl skips itself on any system other than Linux. The rotation
# runs only on the box. go.yml runs the test.
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestSigningKeyRotationKeysFromOpenSSL

# The signing key rotation's owner and group test gives files to other
# owners and groups, which needs root. The macOS runner runs the tests
# without root, so it skips itself. go.yml runs it as root.
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestSigningKeyRotationKeepsOwnersAndGroupsAsRoot

# The signing key rotation wrapper's test of code that another account owns
# gives files to other accounts, which needs root. The macOS runner runs the
# tests without root, so it skips itself. go.yml runs it as root.
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestSigningKeyRotationWrapperRefusesCodeOfAnotherOwnerAsRoot

# The signing key rotation's tests of a file bound over a config or the
# index in a service's mount namespace, and of a --host-root that is a bind
# mount of /, make mounts, which needs root and Linux mount namespaces. The
# macOS runner runs the tests without root, so they skip themselves. go.yml
# runs them as root.
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestSigningKeyRotationSeesTheFilesEachServiceSeesAsRoot
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestSigningKeyRotationHostRootBoundToSlashIsTheHostAsRoot

# The supported-local renderer's signing key tests source
# scripts/72_supported_local_setup.sh, which runs on Linux; a Mac runs it in
# its Lima guest. Both tests skip themselves on any other system. go.yml runs
# the first, and runs the second as root.
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestSupportedLocalRendererKeepsTheSigningKeysPrivate
skips-itself execution-substrate/scripts TestSupportedLocalRendererRefusesASigningKeyFileAnotherUserOwns
